CONTEXT
=======
A C++ program /workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test7.cpp was ported to pure Rust (std only, edition 2021) in /output.
The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test7_executable (compiled with the real mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x; the
header source itself is NOT on disk and must NOT be sought out - treat it as a black box).

The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

Rust port layout:
  /output/Cargo.toml
  /output/test7.rs            entry point (uses #[path] module decls so both 'rustc test7.rs' and cargo work)
  /output/src/cli.rs          atoi
  /output/src/spiral.rs       spiral point generation
  /output/src/earcut/mod.rs   Earcut struct, run(), linkedList, filterPoints, earcutLinked, isEar, isEarHashed,
                              cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut, eliminateHoles/Hole, findHoleBridge
  /output/src/earcut/geom.rs  area, equals, pointInTriangle, sign, onSegment, intersects, intersectsPolygon,
                              locallyInside, middleInside, isValidDiagonal, sectorContainsSector, getLeftmost,
                              splitPolygon, removeNode
  /output/src/earcut/node.rs  Node + NIL sentinel (arena indices replace Node*)
  /output/src/earcut/zorder.rs zOrder, indexCurve, sortLinked

Prebuilt binaries already exist: /output/test7 (rustc -O) and /output/target/release/test7 (cargo).
Already established by the lead engineer (do not redo, but you may spot-check):
  - byte-identical output for every n in 0..=200 and for n in {201,250,299,300,301,400,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000}
  - spiral coordinates are bit-identical f64 (glibc sincos vs Rust sin/cos) for n in {7,41,137,1000,4001}
  - arg edge cases match: no arg, "", " ", "abc", "3x", " 4", "+5", "-5", "-0", "007", "  -12abc",
    "2147483647", "-2147483648", "99999999999999999999", "0x10", "\t9", "1e3"

DO NOT EDIT ANY FILES. You are read-only: investigate and report. The lead engineer applies fixes.


ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION (lens: reproduce-it)
=====
A reviewer auditing the Rust port claims:

  file: /output/src/earcut/geom.rs:167
  severity: minor
  summary: sector_contains_sector uses the wrong third operand in both area terms: `area(m.prev, m, p)` and `area(p.next, m, m.prev)` instead of earcut.hpp's `area(m->prev, m, p->prev)` and `area(p->next, m, m->next)`.
  failure scenario: Reachable only through find_hole_bridge (/output/src/earcut/mod.rs:588), i.e. a polygon with at least one hole. With a hole whose bridge search hits the tie branch `tan_cur == tan_min && !(px > m.x)`, the predicate is evaluated on the wrong vertices: e.g. when the candidate p coincides positionally with m, `area(m.prev, m, p)` is identically 0.0 so the ported predicate returns false where the reference can return true, selecting a different bridge vertex and hence a different triangulation. test7 pushes a single ring, so points[1..] is empty, eliminate_holes/find_hole_bridge never run, and this cannot diverge for any n against test7_executable (re-checked byte-identical for n=7,41,137,500).

Your job is to REFUTE this claim. Read the actual code at that location. Try hard to ACTUALLY REPRODUCE the divergence by running /output/test7 and /workspace/dataset/test7_executable with inputs that should trigger it, or by writing a throwaway harness in /tmp that includes the /output modules via #[path]. If you cannot make the two binaries disagree, and cannot construct a concrete polygon input for which the Rust module and the documented C++ semantics differ, the claim is refuted. Default to refuted=true when uncertain. Set reproduced_divergence=true ONLY if you personally observed the two implementations disagree. DO NOT EDIT FILES under /output.

I read the code, instrumented a copy, built a reference-semantics variant, and fuzzed. Here is what I found.

## The code as written

`/output/src/earcut/geom.rs:164-168`:
```rust
pub(super) fn sector_contains_sector(&self, m: usize, p: usize) -> bool {
    let mp = self.nodes[m].prev;
    let pn = self.nodes[p].next;
    self.area(mp, m, p) < 0.0 && self.area(pn, m, mp) < 0.0
}
```
earcut.hpp/earcut.js 2.2.x is `area(m->prev, m, p->prev) < 0 && area(p->next, m, m->next) < 0`. Both third operands are wrong: `p` instead of `p->prev`, and `m->prev` (reusing the already-bound `mp`) instead of `m->next`. The reviewer's transcription of the defect is exact.

## Reachability — the reviewer is also right here

Sole caller is `/output/src/earcut/mod.rs:588`, inside `find_hole_bridge`, reached only via `eliminate_holes`, which `run()` guards with `if points.len() > 1` (`/output/src/earcut/mod.rs:104`). `/output/test7.rs` pushes exactly one ring, so `points.len() == 1` always.

Empirically: I copied the modules to `/tmp/av`, added `eprintln!` probes at the top of `eliminate_holes`, `find_hole_bridge`, and `sector_contains_sector`, and ran n from -20 through 400 plus {500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000,4001,5000}. Zero hits, all 430 runs.

## No binary divergence — I could not reproduce one

- `/output/test7` vs `/workspace/dataset/test7_executable`: byte-identical for n in -30..=500 plus {600,750,1000,1500,2000,3000,4001} and for the arg edge cases. 0 diffs.
- I built `/tmp/fix/test7_fixed`, an otherwise-identical copy whose predicate uses the reference operands. It is byte-identical to both the shipped Rust binary and the C++ binary across that same sweep. The predicate is dead code for this program; you can flip it either way and nothing moves.

So `reproduced_divergence = false`.

## But the defect is not vacuous — I did construct a diverging polygon

Your refutation criterion has two prongs, and the second one fails. Compiling the `/output` modules unchanged (`/tmp/orig/fz2`) versus the reference-operand variant (`/tmp/fix/fz2`) and feeding both hole-bearing polygons, they disagree:

```
outer = [[0,1], [1,0], [2,2], [0,1], [0,2]]
hole  = [[2,0], [2,0], [2,1]]

shipped /output code   -> [1, 2, 3]
earcut.hpp semantics   -> [1, 2, 0]
```

Broader fuzzing (2-4 rings, 3-10 vertices, integer grids that force `tan_cur == tan_min` ties) diverges on every seed and every coordinate mode I tried, within a few thousand iterations. The wrong operands genuinely select a different bridge vertex and a different triangulation.

I could not run this through the C++ side — `test7_executable` only triangulates the single-ring spiral and the header is not on disk — so the "earcut.hpp semantics" column is the reference formula as the reviewer and I both state it, not an observed C++ run.

## Verdict

I cannot refute this. The finding is factually correct on all three of its assertions: wrong operands, hole-only reachability, and no possible test7 divergence. It is a real fidelity bug in a module the port ships, correctly self-scoped as unobservable for this binary, and correctly graded minor. The fix is a two-token change at `/output/src/earcut/geom.rs:167`.

Throwaway artifacts left in `/tmp/av`, `/tmp/orig`, `/tmp/fix`. Nothing under `/output` was modified. Note: `/tmp/probe` was pre-existing from an earlier session and my first `cp -r` nested a copy inside its `src/`; I abandoned it and used clean dirs, but you may want to delete it.
